items.title: Robotics 1 · Session 42 · LED Blinking
items.symptom: The LED never seems to turn off — it just stays on.
items.answer: The wait 1 seconds after digital write pin 8 to LOW is missing, so the LED is off for only a few microseconds — too short to see. Add the wait back.

items.title: Robotics 2 · Session 43 · Traffic Light System
items.symptom: Yellow and red are on together, and after the first round yellow never goes off.
items.answer: digital write pin 9 to LOW is missing after the yellow wait. Two lights on together usually means a missing LOW before the next HIGH.

items.title: Robotics 3 · Session 44 · Buzzer + Fire Alarm
items.symptom: The alarm rings all the time — and stops when there IS a flame.
items.answer: The if checks digital read pin 2 = 1, but most flame modules give 0 when they see a flame (and 1 when they don't). Change 1 to 0 — or check your own module, since a few work the other way.

items.title: Robotics 4 · Sessions 45–46 · Servo Motor Project
items.symptom: The servo sweeps up to 180° once, then stops moving for ever.
items.answer: The second repeat says change angle by 1, so the angle keeps growing past 180 (the servo can't go further). It should be change angle by -1 to come back.

items.title: Robotics 5 · Session 47 · Ultrasonic Distance Sensor
items.symptom: The distance never changes, however you move your hand.
items.answer: set distance to (distance in cm…) is above the forever loop, so it measures once at the start. Move it inside the loop.

items.title: Robotics 6 · Sessions 48–49 · Flagship synthesis · Automatic Parking Barrier
items.symptom: The gate opens when there is nothing in front of it at all.
items.answer: With no echo the sensor gives 0, and 0 < 15, so the gate opens. Check distance > 0 and distance < 15.

items.title: Robotics 7 · Session 50 · Automatic Street Light
items.symptom: The street light is on in the daytime and off at night.
items.answer: The if says light > 400, but with the LDR on the 5V side, darkness gives a low number. It should be light < 400. (If your LDR is wired the other way round, the opposite is right — always check the readings first.)
